provenance: Assistant translation of the original 20 Vietnamese questions and reference answers; simulated local benchmark, not independently human-certified
labels: Expected source-file labels inherited and filename-mapped from VN. These are not answer-bearing passage labels. Missing README remains missing; no new policy README was invented.

cases.question: What version and date does the current VietStyle Commerce policy set have, and what is its approval status?
cases.reference_answer: Version v1.0, dated 16/10/2026; SIMULATION_DRAFT / simulated document. Business-owner approval is required before real-world use.

cases.question: Who has primary responsibility for KPIs, inventory thresholds, exceptions, and policy approval?
cases.reference_answer: Inventory Manager.

cases.question: How often should classes A, B, and C be cycle-counted, and what criterion determines the ABC classification?
cases.reference_answer: Class A: weekly, approximately 80% of annual consumption value; class B: monthly, approximately the next 15%; class C: quarterly, the remaining approximately 5%. Classification uses annual consumption value (annual demand multiplied by cost), not sales volume alone.

cases.question: When a customer returns an item, what status must it pass through before it can be added to available inventory?
cases.reference_answer: Place returns in QUARANTINE for Returns QA inspection and classification. Add them to available-to-promise only after QA confirms their condition and disposition.

cases.question: Which inventory KPIs must be monitored regularly under the policy set?
cases.reference_answer: Fill rate, stockout rate, inventory record accuracy, days of supply, aged/slow-moving stock, and PO adherence.

cases.question: How far in advance of a campaign must the team prepare its inventory plan, and what information must it check?
cases.reference_answer: At least 4 weeks before the campaign. Forecast by SKU/size/color; check inventory, POs, lead time, MOQ, campaign dates, channel, discount, minimum-order conditions, and stackable_flag. Increasing target stock requires a forecast or approval.

cases.question: What actions are required when days of supply exceeds 120 days and when it exceeds 180 days?
cases.reference_answer: Above 120 days: pause replenishment and review the forecast, size/color inventory, in-transit goods, and campaigns. Above 180 days: prepare an approved handling plan such as transfers, bundles, controlled markdowns, or disposal.

cases.question: Are the 14-day lead time, 7 safety days, and 7-day review period verified real-world values from the dataset?
cases.reference_answer: No. These are assumed default simulation parameters. Replace or calibrate them using supplier data and obtain business-owner approval.

cases.question: Using the formulas in the documents, if average demand is 10 units per day and the default parameters apply, what are the ROP and Target Stock?
cases.reference_answer: ROP = 10 x (14 + 7) = 210 units. Target Stock = 10 x (14 + 7 + 7) = 280 units. These are illustrative results using assumed parameters.

cases.question: How is inventory position calculated? If on-hand is 120, open PO is 40, and backorder is 25, what is the inventory position?
cases.reference_answer: Inventory Position = On-hand + Open PO - Backorder = 120 + 40 - 25 = 135 units.

cases.question: A SKU has a stockout signal but calculated days of supply is 145 days. What should the AI Agent do before recommending another purchase?
cases.reference_answer: Mark DATA CONFLICT and temporarily block automatic PO recommendations. Check available inventory, held stock, unshipped orders/backorders, transactions, the snapshot timestamp, and the days-of-supply formula. Reopen the replenishment decision only after the Inventory Controller records a conclusion.

cases.question: Both stockout_flag and overstock_flag are enabled for a SKU. Can we conclude it is definitely both understocked and overstocked? What should the system do?
cases.reference_answer: The two flags alone do not establish that conclusion. Treat them as conflicting signals: set DATA CONFLICT, block automatic POs, and verify transactions, snapshots, pending orders, available inventory, and demand/days-of-supply calculations.

cases.question: Describe the inventory-count variance handling process from preparation through ticket closure, including the mandatory controls.
cases.reference_answer: Export the SKU/location list and snapshot; prepare and freeze transactions or record transactions during counting; count independently (blind count where applicable); have a second person recount variances; reconcile receipts, picks, shipments, returns, transfers, cancellations, and transactions pending synchronization; investigate the cause; document and obtain independent approval; update through an auditable transaction; synchronize and update the exception report before closing the ticket.

cases.question: Who may perform the count, enter an adjustment, and approve it? May the same person perform all three roles?
cases.reference_answer: Separate duties: the counter, adjustment-entry person, and approver must be different people. Approval must be independent. Small variances with evidence require Inventory Controller/Supervisor approval; large, recurring, or above-threshold variances require the Inventory Manager and Finance/Operations as appropriate.

cases.question: What minimum information must be retained for an inventory adjustment transaction?
cases.reference_answer: Ticket ID, policy ID, SKU, before/after quantities, reason code, evidence, data-entry person, and approver. Count records also need the timestamp, counter, and Adjustment Transaction ID. Do not delete old transactions or directly edit source files.

cases.question: QA classifies three batches of returned goods as A-grade, B-grade, and C-grade. How should each class be handled?
cases.reference_answer: A-grade may return to sale after QA confirmation; B-grade may be repaired/repackaged if approved; C-grade stays segregated for supplier return, scrapping, or write-off. None may enter available inventory before QA confirms disposition.

cases.question: An employee discovers a SKU suspected of being counterfeit or seriously mislabeled. May it still be sold if the system records stock on hand?
cases.reference_answer: No. Immediately set HOLD/QUARANTINE; do not sell or include it in available-to-promise until QA/Operations decides disposition. For suspected fraud or loss, quarantine the SKU, preserve evidence, and notify Compliance/Operations.

cases.question: According to the dataset, what are the current inbound PO and backorder quantities for SKU X? Provide the exact numbers.
cases.reference_answer: The described documents/dataset cannot establish those quantities: complete inbound PO and backorder data are unavailable. Obtain additional data or query an authorized system source; do not invent numbers.

cases.question: What is the latest inventory snapshot date in the Datathon dataset? Can it be used to claim what the current inventory is today?
cases.reference_answer: The latest snapshot is 31/12/2022. It is not current inventory. State the snapshot date and request current data before making operational decisions.

cases.question: A user asks the AI Agent to create and issue a PO immediately when inventory position is less than or equal to ROP. May the agent do this? Explain the limits and appropriate workflow.
cases.reference_answer: No. The agent may only read authorized data and answer/recommend with source citations and the snapshot date; it must not issue POs or adjust inventory autonomously. The Planner prepares a proposal and checks open POs, backorders, MOQ, and budget; Procurement/the authorized approver approves before issuance. If data conflicts, block the automatic recommendation and refer it to the Inventory Controller.
